item.title: China urges non-regional countries to stop meddling in South China Sea issue: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
China urges non-regional countries to stop meddling in South China Sea issue: spokesperson BEIJING, Nov. 26 (Xinhua) -- China on Thursday urged certain non-regional countries to respect its sovereignty and rights and interests and stop interfering in the South China Sea issue. The Philippines and Australia recently signed a defense cooperation agreement, which the Philippine side claimed would bolster the Philippines' credible deterrent posture in the South China Sea to counter China's actions. Asked to make comment at a regular press conference on Thursday, Chen Xi, a spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense, said certain Filipino politicians, driven by personal interests, have been spreading false narratives about China, stirring up trouble, and seeking to rope in outside forces to back them up and make waves. Such moves will only escalate tensions and undermine regional stability, Chen said. "The South China Sea should be a sea of peace, friendship and cooperation. Stoking troubles and provoking confrontation are not welcome here," he said. The spokesperson urged relevant non-regional countries to earnestly respect China's sovereignty and rights and interests in the South China Sea and cease meddling in the issue. China's actions to safeguard its territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests are legitimate and justified, Chen said, adding that China will continue to take necessary measures to respond firmly to provocations and infringement activities. China will resolutely thwart any attempt to destabilize the South China Sea, Chen said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: China firmly opposes U.S. additional tariffs on China, other economies: commerce ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
China firmly opposes U.S. additional tariffs on China, other economies: commerce ministry BEIJING, Nov. 26 (Xinhua) -- China firmly opposes the imposition of additional Section 301 tariffs by the United States on China and other economies, a Ministry of Commerce spokesperson said on Thursday. The Office of the United States Trade Representative recently announced the results of its Section 301 investigation into alleged "overcapacity," proposing to impose additional Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, including China. Spokesperson He Yadong said at a regular press briefing that the U.S. Section 301 investigation is a typical act of unilateralism that seriously disrupts the international economic order and violates World Trade Organization rules. He noted that a certain country is using the pretext of "overcapacity" to pursue protectionism, politicizing normal market competition and turning industrial development issues into political tools. Such practices do little to address its own structural imbalances, but will instead disrupt the stability and security of global industrial and supply chains, undermine industrial cooperation, push up global inflation, harm the interests of businesses and consumers, and pose long-term systemic risks to global economic growth, he added. The spokesperson urged the United States to correct its erroneous practices and return to the right track of resolving differences through dialogue and consultation. China will closely monitor the developments and reserves the right to take necessary measures to firmly safeguard its legitimate rights and interests, he added. Responding to another media query on the arrangement for a 30-billion-U.S. dollar reciprocal tariff reduction reached by China and the United States in September, He noted that China believes its early implementation would help expand bilateral trade. "We noticed that the United States had exempted products covered by the arrangement from the scope of its proposed Section 301 measures targeting alleged overcapacity," the spokesperson said. "We hope the United States will expedite its internal procedures and work with China to bring the 30-billion-U.S. dollar reciprocal tariff reduction arrangement into effect at an early date," he added. item.title: Global delegates discuss water governance at millennia-old living heritage site in southwest China
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
Global delegates discuss water governance at millennia-old living heritage site in southwest China CHENGDU, Nov. 26 (Xinhua) -- The main forum of the Dujiangyan River Strategy Forum opened Thursday in the city of Dujiangyan, southwest China's Sichuan Province, drawing about 200 scholars, officials and other delegates from home and abroad, organizers said. Gathered in the city, known for the Dujiangyan irrigation system that was built around 256 BC and remains in use today as part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the representatives exchanged river management plans, devised strategies for ensuring water security, and promoted mutual learning among global civilizations. A think tank report on Chinese wisdom in river governance as seen from Dujiangyan was also unveiled at the forum. The report noted that the Dujiangyan irrigation system is the only ancient water conservancy project in the world still in use and one of the earliest successful practices of harmonious coexistence between humanity and nature. Its construction fully reflects the Chinese nation's spirit of unremitting self-improvement, fearlessness in the face of difficulties, and pioneering endeavor. It highlighted the wisdom embodied in the ancient project, such as adapting measures to local conditions, following natural trends, harmony between man and nature, and managing water for the benefit of the people. The report was co-authored by the Xinhua Institute, a national high-level think tank affiliated with Xinhua News Agency, and the publicity and education center of the Ministry of Water Resources. Hu Yun, vice governor of Sichuan, said in his address that the province invested 286.9 billion yuan (around 42.76 billion U.S. dollars) in water conservancy from 2021 to 2025, with the ecological protection and governance of rivers and lakes seeing historic improvement. The province will seize opportunities to fully promote the construction of water network pilot zones and backbone water network projects, and strive to contribute more to the practice of water conservancy quality development, Hu added. Huo Xiaoguang, vice president of Xinhua News Agency, said the agency will fully leverage its advantages to better tell the story of China's water management in the new era to the world, share China's experience in river governance, and promote exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations around the globe. Xinhua will also aim to turn Dujiangyan into a window for the world to understand China, thus contributing Chinese wisdom and solutions to global water governance, he noted. Liu Dongshun, vice minister of water resources, said that since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China in 2012, the country has greatly enhanced its capacity to prevent floods and droughts, further optimized its water resources allocation, and fundamentally improved the overall condition of its rivers and lakes. Philippe Gourbesville, president of the International Association for Hydro-Environment Engineering and Research, said the Chinese government has clear goals and firm determination, and stands as an excellent model of river management internationally. He added that China has efficiently implemented many solutions, like establishing a system of river chiefs to coordinate action and management, while effectively managing and utilizing important water conservancy infrastructure, giving full play to its role in agricultural irrigation and river transport. China's rich experience can serve as a source of insights for France and other European countries, Gourbesville noted. At the main forum, attendees also saw the release of an initiative calling for safeguarding water security, protecting river ecology, using technologies for river governance, channeling cooperation to pool wisdom for global governance, and fulfilling the promise to manage water for the benefit of the people. The forum featured a main forum, a sub-forum and supporting activities, including on-site inspection of the Dujiangyan irrigation system and exhibitions showcasing achievements and innovative practices in China's river governance. The event was co-hosted by Xinhua News Agency Sichuan Branch and the Sichuan Provincial Water Resources Department. After more than two thousand years of continuous protection and iterative development, the Dujiangyan irrigation district, the country's largest, has expanded to 11.945 million mu (roughly 796,333 hectares), stably guaranteeing water security for production and daily life for 32 million people. item.title: High-speed rails in China's Yangtze River Delta top 8,500 km as three new lines open
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
Home>>
High-speed rails in China's Yangtze River Delta top 8,500 km as three new lines open (Xinhua) 11:20, November 27, 2026 BEIJING, Nov. 27 (Xinhua) -- Three high-speed railways opened in east China's Anhui Province on Friday, expanding the high-speed rail network in the Yangtze River Delta to more than 8,500 km. The new lines, which add about 364.5 km of new mainline tracks with a design speed of 350 km per hour, will improve regional connectivity by creating multiple fast routes linking major cities. The expanded network will serve one of China's most vibrant economic regions. The Yangtze River Delta, comprising Shanghai and the provinces of Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui, accounted for nearly a quarter of the country's GDP in 2025. item.title: New growth drivers fuel China's industrial profit gains
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
New growth drivers fuel China's industrial profit gains BEIJING, Nov. 27 (Xinhua) -- Profits of China's industrial firms above designated size rose 16 percent year on year in the first 10 months of 2026, official data showed Friday, as new growth drivers gathered momentum. The growth rate accelerated 0.5 percentage points from the January-September period, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS). In October alone, profits surged 20.1 percent year on year, accelerating 5.7 percentage points from September. By sector, mining profits jumped 38.8 percent and manufacturing profits rose 17.5 percent, while profits in the production and supply of electricity, heat, gas and water fell 14.8 percent. The electronics sector was a standout driver, with profits increasing 100 percent year on year in the first 10 months and contributing 9.7 percentage points to overall industrial profit growth, as surging demand for AI computing power fueled profits in memory chips and related manufacturing. Within computer manufacturing, profits of computer makers surged 410 percent and those of computer peripheral makers jumped 200 percent. High-tech manufacturing also shone, with profits up 50.9 percent year on year in the first 10 months, outpacing overall industrial growth by 34.9 percentage points. Driven by large-scale construction of intelligent computing centers, profits of optical fiber and optical cable makers surged 670 percent and 150 percent, respectively. The profit margin on operating revenue stood at 5.69 percent, up 0.45 percentage points year on year. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Chengdu: Where poetry flows through everyday life
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
Chengdu: Where poetry flows through everyday life German poet and painter Margarete Werner reads at home. (Photo/Dai Guangyu) The Minjiang River has carved its path through the landscape for millennia, but it was human ingenuity that truly tamed it. The Dujiangyan irrigation system, engineered over two thousand years ago in southwest China's Sichuan province, channels the river's waters across the fertile Chengdu Plain. For centuries, this marvel of hydraulic engineering has shielded the region from catastrophic floods and prolonged droughts, laying the foundation for what became known as the "Land of Abundance." Long before modern infrastructure, Sichuan attracted scholars and poets, earning the enduring belief that the land itself inspires verse. Chengdu holds a rare distinction in Chinese history: it has occupied the same site and kept the same name for roughly three thousand years. Today, it stands as a living testament to this continuity -- a metropolis where deep-rooted traditions and dynamic innovation thrive side by side. Nestled among the misty peaks of Qingcheng Mountain, a quiet cottage belongs to Margarete Werner, a German painter and poet who goes by the Chinese name Lei Zhen. Inside, floor-to-ceiling shelves hold Chinese classics alongside Western literary works, reflecting a mind shaped by two cultures. Surrounded by emerald hills and terraced tea gardens, she finds inspiration at the intersection of Eastern and Western thought. Werner grew up in the foothills of the Alps. Ink and wash paintings collected by her grandmother first introduced her to the aesthetics of the East. At 19, while studying in London, she happened upon Chinese classics in a bookstore in Chinatown. From then on, she felt drawn to this distant land. After graduation, she moved to China, eventually settling on Qingcheng Mountain with her husband to focus fully on her writing. "I've always felt that Li Bai is a profoundly universal poet. His verses speak directly to the human experience, transcending time and borders," she said. She often recites poetry while hiking mountain trails. One line from Li Bai's Dulu Pian resonates deeply with her: "A bright moon shines straight down, revealing all without concealment." Its unguarded honesty mirrors the tranquil, grounded life she has cultivated here. Sichuan has long had a close connection with poetry. Famous Chinese poets Du Fu, Li Bai, and Lu You all composed celebrated works in Chengdu, helping shape the city's cultural character. For Werner, however, the city's poetic spirit is not confined to the pages of books. It is also alive in everyday speech. Residents still use words like luo yu (falling rain) and niao huan (birds singing), preserving the musicality of ancient Chinese in daily conversation. "Standing at the foot of Qingcheng Mountain, I feel that the rhythms of Tang and Song poetry have returned to their original form," Werner said. This poetic atmosphere extends beyond literature. Since the launch of the Chengdu International Poetry Week in 2017, more than 110 foreign poets from over 50 countries and regions have visited the city to seek inspiration. Their works offer glimpses of Chengdu through the eyes of foreign poets, with some featured in a collection titled "A city in the depths of time: Chengdu through the eyes of foreign poets." An aerial view of Jincheng Lake in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan province. (Photo/Jiang Xiaoyi) To Werner, "poetry is like green bamboo, with the vitality to pierce through concrete." A relaxed lifestyle and an inclusive, open-minded spirit are among Chengdu's most appealing qualities. James Ayala, a young American and conservation biology expert at the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding, has spent years studying giant pandas in the city. Along the way, he has picked up a remarkably authentic Sichuan-accented Mandarin. Familiar with the characteristics of individual giant pandas, Ayala can tell them apart by their nose prints and gait. He has also taken part in habitat improvement and giant panda conservation research. He has received both the Tianfu Friendship Award and the Jinsha Friendship Award, which recognize foreign experts for their outstanding contributions to Sichuan and Chengdu, respectively. He also served as a torchbearer at the World Games 2025 in Chengdu. In his spare time, Ayala loves exploring the city's streets and alleys. The Chunxi Road commercial area is bustling with activity, with the iconic giant panda sculpture at Chengdu International Finance Square, the traditional tiled roofs and eaves of Taikoo Li shopping center, glasses-free 3D screens, and traditional markets all within easy reach of one another. Modern trends blend seamlessly with the charm of the city's historical heritage here. The auspicious animal carvings on the ancient buildings of Wenshu Monastery reflect the Chinese ideal of harmony between humanity and nature. When he needs a break from walking, Ayala likes to find an old teahouse, settle into a bamboo chair, sip tea from a lidded bowl, and watch Sichuan opera. At local restaurants, he often asks the chef to add a little more chili. Photo shows an aerial view of a section of Tianfu Greenway in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan province. (Photo courtesy of Chengdu Tianfu Greenway Construction Investment Group Co., Ltd.) Chengdu continues to develop as a park city, with more than 10,000 kilometers of Tianfu Greenway connecting parks and green spaces across the city. The city's urban renewal projects follow the principle of avoiding large-scale demolition and reconstruction, while preserving the original layout and vitality of established neighborhoods. Its relaxed and inclusive atmosphere has attracted a growing number of foreigners who choose to settle in the city. Chengdu is also fertile ground for creativity and innovation. Its rich cultural heritage provides fertile soil for Chinese-style cultural intellectual property, from which the "Ne Zha" animated film series has emerged. At the same time, the city has brought together extensive scientific and technological resources, with emerging industries such as robotics, artificial intelligence (AI), and advanced manufacturing gaining momentum. Amin Naboureh, a young Iranian, came to Chengdu in pursuit of his dream of studying mountains. He is now an associate research fellow at the Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment, Chinese Academy of Sciences, in Chengdu. Amin Naboureh, an Iranian associate research fellow at the Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment, Chinese Academy of Sciences, takes part in a public fitness running event at Xinglong Lake in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan province. (Photo courtesy of the interviewee) Hossin Md Altab, a young Bangladeshi, teaches at the Entrepreneurship College of Chengdu University and is also an entrepreneur. He developed a smart Chinese language learning platform, which combines AI with Chinese-language learning to provide digital learning tools for learners from different countries. The platform now has more than 30,000 registered users. "Whether Chinese or foreign, anyone with a good idea can find plenty of opportunities and platforms for development in Chengdu," he said. By providing an open platform and bringing together creative talent from China and abroad, the city has created an environment where diverse ideas meet and take shape. From a cradle of classical verse to a forward-looking metropolis, Chengdu welcomes the world with its poetic charm, relaxed rhythm, and relentless creativity. Here, people of different backgrounds and ambitions come together to build their lives. As the bilingual American poet Jami Proctor Xu once wrote: "If I tell everyone I meet that Chengdu is my paradise, all of the above is why." James Ayala, a young American and conservation biology expert at the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding, conducts behavioral training for a giant panda. (Photo courtesy of the interviewee) Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: World's longest underwater shield-built highway tunnel reaches milestone in east China
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
World's longest underwater shield-built highway tunnel reaches milestone in east China This photo taken on Nov. 26, 2026 shows the construction site of the Haitai Yangtze River Tunnel in east China's Jiangsu Province. China's self-developed tunnel boring machine (TBM) "Jianghai," with a maximum excavation diameter of 16.64 meters, has completed the 7.46-km tunneling work in the water section of Yangtze River on Thursday and successfully landed in Taicang of Jiangsu Province, marking that the right line of the Haitai Yangtze River Tunnel has been drilled through the Yangtze River. Stretching approximately 39.07 kilometers in total, Haitai Yangtze River Tunnel, connecting Haimen of Nantong to the north and Taicang of Suzhou to the south, is designed as a six-lane, bidirectional highway with a design speed of 100 kilometers per hour. (Xinhua/Ji Chunpeng) NANJING, Nov. 26 (Xinhua) -- The right-hand bore of the Haitai Yangtze River Tunnel, the world's longest underwater shield-built highway tunnel, crossed beneath the Yangtze River on Thursday, becoming the first of the tunnel's two bores to reach the south bank. The country's self-developed tunneling machine completed the 7.46-km under-river stretch. The tunnel boring machine, named Jianghai, has a maximum excavation diameter of 16.64 meters. It began digging from the north bank in April 2025 and entered the under-river section that September. The crossing took about 14 months, with the machine advancing an average of 20 meters a day, according to Meng Defeng, who oversees shield tunneling for China Railway 14th Bureau Group on the project. The tunnel is a key step in building a major trans-river road link under China's longest river, connecting Haimen in Nantong with Taicang in Suzhou, both in east China's Jiangsu Province. Stretching approximately 39.07 kilometers in total, the tunnel includes an 11.185-kilometer underwater section made up of two parallel bores. Once open, the tunnel will shorten journeys from Nantong to southern Jiangsu and Shanghai, improving road connections across the Yangtze River Delta. China issued a plan in July this year to comprehensively advance the high-quality development of integrated transport services during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), the Ministry of Transport announced. The plan aims to largely establish a modern integrated transport service system by 2030. Under the plan, China will improve connections among different modes of transport, make passenger transfers more convenient and enhance freight logistics services. It will also promote the integration of transport and tourism, improve services at transport hubs, and strengthen rural passenger transport, freight and delivery services. item.title: China's high-standard opening up creates new opportunities for global cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
China's high-standard opening up creates new opportunities for global cooperation BEIJING, Nov. 26 (Xinhua) -- At Friendship Pass on the China-Vietnam border in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, an improved customs inspection system has cut the time needed to identify pests in imported fruit to 36 hours or less, down from three to five days. This port handled durian imports worth 17.61 billion yuan (about 2.62 billion U.S. dollars) in the first eight months of 2026, up 27.9 percent year on year, with China and Vietnam now jointly developing a smart border port to further facilitate cross-border trade. These efforts reflect China's broader push to expand high-standard opening up and develop new competitive advantages, a theme explored in the latest episode of China Economic Roundtable, an all-media talk show hosted by Xinhua News Agency. A drone photo taken on Sept. 3, 2026 shows a view of the Qinzhou Port in Qinzhou City, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. (Xinhua/Cao Yiming) BROADENING THE SCOPE OF OPENING UP Despite a complex external environment, China's goods imports and exports grew 20 percent year on year in the first 10 months of 2026. Imports rose 23.6 percent, continuing to outpace export growth amid China's ongoing efforts to advance voluntary and unilateral opening up. The country's trading partners are becoming increasingly diverse. In the first three quarters of the year, China's goods trade with Belt and Road partner countries rose 17.1 percent year on year, accounting for 51 percent of its total trade in goods. Expanding into emerging markets has helped mitigate risks arising from slowing demand and mounting trade barriers in some traditional markets, making China's foreign trade more resilient, said Zhang Yan, a researcher at a research center under the National Development and Reform Commission. In northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, trade with Belt and Road partner countries surged 35.3 percent year on year in the first nine months, according to Li Kaiyi, head of Yinchuan Customs. To overcome the region's geographical constraints, local customs authorities have piloted a new customs supervision model for rail-sea intermodal transport, boosting logistics efficiency by more than 30 percent. Local customs authorities have also helped wine producers resolve difficulties in obtaining certificates for exports to the European Union, with the value of Ningxia's wine exports to Germany and Spain more than tripling in the first three quarters of 2026, Li said. Wooden barrels are seen at a wine cellar of Xige Estate in Qingtongxia, northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, Sept. 23, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Yun) The potential for cooperation extends beyond the wine industry. Speaking in Ningxia, New Zealand's ambassador to China pointed to opportunities for technical exchanges between the two countries in wine production, livestock farming and crop cultivation. China's opening up is also creating new opportunities for foreign investors. In Hainan Province in south China, the number of newly established foreign-invested enterprises rose 31.1 percent year on year in the first nine months of 2026, with new projects including a Siemens Energy gas turbine assembly base and service center, said Wang Fengli, deputy director of the Office of the Free Trade Port Working Committee of the Communist Party of China Hainan Provincial Committee. DEVELOPING NEW COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGES China's advances in science and technology and the development of its digital economy are also creating new opportunities for international economic cooperation. From drone-based crop-protection services for cotton fields in Central Asia, to the international expansion of domestically developed smart in-vehicle systems, more Chinese companies are moving beyond individual product exports to providing integrated technological solutions and services, Zhang said. The country's exports of knowledge-intensive services grew 11.7 percent year on year to 1.2 trillion yuan in the first three quarters of 2026, accounting for 53.7 percent of its total services exports. Opening-up policies are also helping develop new businesses in high-value-added services. In Hainan, for instance, bonded maintenance and expedited customs clearance can reduce aircraft maintenance costs for foreign airlines by around 10 percent to 15 percent, Wang said. Staff members work at an aircraft maintenance base of Grand China Aviation Maintenance Co., Ltd. at the Haikou Airport comprehensive bonded zone in Haikou, south China's Hainan Province, Oct. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Xin Yuewei) Meanwhile, digital cultural products, including online literature, video games and online dramas, are another growing area in China's services exports, Zhang noted. In Hainan's Chengmai County, a public service platform helps game developers overcome barriers to international expansion, such as cross-border network latency, regulatory compliance and payment settlement. The platform has attracted 125 enterprises and has more than 40 million registered overseas users. Under the policies of the Hainan Free Trade Port (FTP) on secure and orderly cross-border data flows, this platform provides dedicated data links, reducing the costs developers would otherwise incur in arranging such connections themselves. DEEPENING INSTITUTIONAL OPENING UP Beyond facilitating the flow of goods and production factors, China is steadily advancing its institutional opening up in terms of rules, regulations, management and standards, seeking closer alignment with high-standard international economic and trade rules. The Hainan FTP serves as a testing ground for such reforms. Following the launch of island-wide special customs operations in December 2025, the share of tariff lines eligible for zero-tariff treatment on qualifying imports increased from 21 percent to 74 percent, Wang said. Vehicles bound for Vietnam are pictured after customs clearance at Youyiguan Port, or Friendship Pass, in Pingxiang City, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, Jan. 28, 2026. (Xinhua/Lu Boan) At the regional level, the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol brings cooperation in the digital economy, green economy and supply chain connectivity into an institutional framework, moving regional cooperation beyond tariff reductions toward greater coordination of rules, Zhang said. Greater openness also requires stronger risk management capabilities, Zhang said, suggesting that pilot free trade zones and free trade ports conduct stress tests in areas like cross-border data flows, financial opening up and cross-border services trade. Looking ahead, the outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) sets out measures to further expand the areas and geographical scope of opening up in an orderly manner, promote innovation in trade, and attract and utilize more foreign investment. "Regardless of changes in the international landscape, China will continue to counter external uncertainties with the certainty of steadily expanding its voluntary opening up," Zhang said, adding that China's high-quality development will create new opportunities for countries around the world.
